info.title: Vendor Service - Basket Optimization and Recurring Baskets
info.description:
Customer shopping optimization: Optimize My Cart, budget shopping, and recurring baskets.

THE RULE THAT GOVERNS EVERY ROUTE: optimization returns a PROPOSAL, and it never silently mutates the customer's cart. Evaluating is free and commits nobody; accepting is a separate, refusable act that creates a NEW cart version and requires an authoritative requote afterwards.

WHAT NONE OF THESE ROUTES DO: create a logistics mission, reserve a provider, reserve stock, create a payment intent, create an order, or charge anybody. Evaluating a hundred candidate baskets creates exactly zero of each - a property of how the service is composed rather than a promise about how it behaves.

NOTHING IS FABRICATED. Every candidate is a real active listing with an authoritative price and authoritative sellable stock. No product, price, stock level, vendor, equivalence or quality score is invented, and when no basket fits a budget the answer says how far short it falls and which constraint is holding it there rather than manufacturing a cheaper one.

THE SEARCH IS BOUNDED and says so. An unbounded search over a catalogue would be a denial-of-service vector wearing an optimizer's name.

post.summary: Find the best basket for a budget and a list of needs
post.description:
Quote-only. Creates no missions, no reservations, no payment intents and no orders.

The budget is evaluated on the FINAL DELIVERED TOTAL - merchandise plus delivery. Returning a basket whose merchandise fits and whose delivered total does not, and calling it a fit, is the specific failure this contract exists to prevent.

A result that fits no budget is returned with 200. It is a successful answer that states the minimum feasible delivered total, the shortfall and the binding constraints.

post.summary: Accept a proposal, creating a new cart version
post.description:
The ONE route in this document that changes the customer's cart.

It takes no body. The proposal identifies the basket and everything about that basket was computed server-side; accepting a client-supplied total or line list would let a customer approve one thing and receive another.

Idempotent. Accepting twice returns the SAME cart version rather than making a second one, so a double-tapped button is harmless. Refused with 409 when the proposal has expired or when the cart moved underneath it - applying it then would discard whatever the customer did in between.

requote_required is always true. The proposal's totals were an estimate against prices and stock at the moment it was built; the authoritative money is the CheckoutQuote produced from the new cart version.

post.description:
Stores REQUIREMENTS AND PREFERENCES, not 'buy exactly these SKUs from these vendors again'. Every occurrence re-evaluates active listings, sellable stock, current prices, eligible vendors and the delivery plan.

The timezone is required and must be an IANA name. 'Every Tuesday at nine' means nine in the customer's morning; a schedule resolved against server-local time drifts with deployments.

An auto-approving policy REQUIRES a spending ceiling. An unbounded standing purchase authority is not a preference this API offers, and the request is refused rather than silently downgraded.

post.description:
Goes through exactly the same claim-first path as the scheduled sweep, so a customer tapping this while the worker is generating the same occurrence still produces ONE generation.

Generating is not ordering. The stages are distinct and each has its own gate: generation, proposal, customer acceptance, cart version, quote, order, payment. This route produces the first two.

422.description: The request could not be understood.

customerBearer.description: Customer Service access token. The customer is taken from the verified subject claim and never from a request body.

Requirement.description: One thing the customer needs. A requirement is a NEED, not a SKU: 'two litres of permitted milk' survives a vendor going out of stock, changing price or leaving the platform, and 'listing lst_9f21 x2' does not.

category_ref.description: A canonical taxonomy node, for a need stated as a need rather than as a product. This is what lets a recurring basket re-shop instead of re-buying a decision made months ago.

quantity.description: Satisfied exactly or reported as unmet. A cheaper basket is never produced by quietly delivering fewer items.

required_brand.description: HARD. No objective, no budget shortfall and no saving may set it aside; a cheaper substitute of another brand is not offered at any price.

minimum_quality_grade.description: HARD. Checkable because the catalogue states which grades a listing offers. Note the asymmetry with the QUALITY_BALANCED objective: a stated grade requirement is checkable, and RANKING two listings by quality is not, because the platform holds no ordinal quality signal.

substitution.description:
Defaults to EXACT_ONLY. The most restrictive value is the default on purpose: a customer who said nothing about substitution has not consented to any.

SAME_PRODUCT_ANY_VENDOR is barely a substitution - the same manufactured article bought at a different shop. EQUIVALENT_PRODUCT additionally permits a different product the taxonomy authority maps to the same canonical node, subject to brand and quality constraints.

Nothing is ever substituted on name similarity. Equivalence comes from a manufacturer trade identifier, the catalogue product identity or the taxonomy authority - never from two products sounding alike.

preferred_brands.description: SOFT. Breaks ties among candidates that already satisfy every hard constraint.

proposal_id.description: Present when this variant was persisted as an acceptable offer.

delivery_total_minor.description: Priced by the quote-only fulfilment planner against real logistics quotes. It is never estimated as a fixed fee per vendor, because delivery is most of the difference between two baskets of the same groceries and a made-up fee would decide the comparison.

final_delivered_total_minor.description: The only number the customer pays, and the only one a budget is evaluated against.

minimum_feasible_delivered_total_minor.description: The cheapest COMPLETE basket satisfying every hard constraint, whatever it costs. Computed from real candidates, and absent when no complete basket exists - quoting a price for something that cannot be bought would be worse than saying nothing.

no_complete_basket.description: At least one requirement cannot be satisfied at ANY price. A different answer from 'too expensive', and kept apart from it.

search_truncated.description: A configured bound stopped the search before every candidate basket was evaluated. Reported rather than hidden: an optimizer that silently truncates and presents its answer as the best available is claiming a thoroughness it does not have.

optimality_note.description: The exact claim this API makes. Not 'the cheapest basket': the search is bounded, so for most inputs some baskets were never looked at, and a stronger word would be a stronger claim than the implementation supports.

quality_variant_unavailable_reason.description: Why no QUALITY_BALANCED variant was produced. The platform holds a quality-grade SELECTION vocabulary for fresh goods and no ordinal quality score for anything, so for most requests this variant genuinely cannot be produced - and inventing a score to fill the slot would be presenting a fabrication as advice.

budget_minor.description: A ceiling on the FINAL DELIVERED total. Omit for no budget.

address_ref.description: The customer's OWN saved-location reference. Raw coordinates are deliberately not accepted: pricing a delivery to an address the caller has no connection to would leak serviceability information about arbitrary points on the map.

quoted_available_quantity.description: Stock AT THE TIME OF QUOTING. Named for what it is: nothing here reserved it, and checkout revalidates it.

equivalence_basis.description: The authority that says these two are interchangeable. There is deliberately no value meaning 'the names looked similar'.

replayed.description: True when this acceptance had already happened and the same cart version is being returned.

approval_policy.description:
Defaults to ALWAYS_ASK. Silence is not consent.

AUTO_VENDOR_CHANGE_WITHIN_CEILING permits a VENDOR change for the SAME product, within the ceiling - the article is unchanged, so the customer receives exactly what they chose from a different shop. No policy permits a different product, a different brand, an unmet quantity or a material price rise without asking.

day_of_month.description: Capped at 28: a monthly basket that silently skipped February would recur less often than the customer was told.

occurrence_key.description: The deterministic identity of one scheduled moment: the local wall-clock time plus its zone. Derived only from the schedule, so a retry, a replay, a restart and a duplicate scheduler delivery all present the same key and collide on a unique index rather than creating a second generation.

state.description: AUTO_APPROVED means the occurrence is inside the bounded preauthorization the customer themselves configured. It creates no order and moves no money.

PlanComparison.description: SAME_VENDOR versus OPTIMIZED, both priced against TODAY's catalogue. The same-vendor side is not last week's receipt: a customer deciding whether to accept a change needs to know what declining it would cost now.
